executiveAssessment.text:
Executive Conclusion. Spice Island Beach Resort's priority is a Reality Gap in how a distinctive part of the proposition is represented in AI answers.

What the Data Is Telling Us. Outdoor Event Space is recognized in only 1.1% of monitored answers. That is low enough to matter commercially if the attribute is part of how the hotel should win relevant traveler needs. Overall scores can hide this concentrated representation miss. Broader Scenario Presence (100%) and Consideration (73.8%) do not, by themselves, prove the distinctive attribute is traveling into answers.

Why It Matters. If distinctive property attributes are weakly represented, the hotel can look broadly visible while still losing the moments where its real proposition should matter. This is a representation problem first, not automatically a peer-competition program.

Where the Pattern Is Concentrated. Business Travel is the softest Scenario Capture at 100.0%, while Business Travel, Leisure Travel, and Group / Meeting show broader coverage. Focus where the gap is concentrated rather than treating every territory equally. Reality Coverage is 37.5% (9 of 24 attributes). Start with gaps that matter operationally — beginning with Swim-Out Suites.

What Management Should Focus On Now. Focus first on Outdoor Event Space. Verify first-party and major travel-source completeness for that attribute before treating the issue as a peer-competition problem. Confirm the attribute is stated clearly where AI systems are most likely to read it.

What Not to Overreact To. No comparable prior official period is available — read these as current levels, not period-over-period change.

What to Review Next. Open Reality Gap evidence for Outdoor Event Space and compare recognition cues with official property pages and high-authority travel sources. Then check a small set of related demand scenarios for whether the attribute appears when competitors are named.

biggestStrength.headline: Often placed near the top when AI ranks hotels
biggestStrength.body: Among AI answers where hotel ranking could be measured, Spice Island Beach Resort appeared in the Top 3 87.5% of the time. This shows how prominently the hotel is positioned when AI includes it.

biggestConstraint.headline: Not appearing consistently in AI answers
biggestConstraint.body: The hotel appeared in at least one AI answer for 100% of the traveler needs we tested, but across all individual AI answers it appeared 73.8% of the time. In practical terms, AI recognizes the hotel as relevant for many types of trips, but a traveler will not consistently see it among the hotel options surfaced.

actionAgenda.actionTitle: Stand up a TripAdvisor management-response program with owner, SLA, and theme tracking — focus: designate accountable owner, set response SLA, identify recurring complaint themes monthly
actionAgenda.observedIssue: TripAdvisor appears in 95.2% of cited sources in the current monitoring period (60 citations), making response quality and factual corrections operationally material when misconceptions appear.
actionAgenda.recommendedAction: Confirm the hotel’s canonical facts for TripAdvisor responses with the accountable owner (Spice Island Beach Resort). Complete the applicable checklist items: designate accountable owner; set response SLA (property-configured; do not invent a default unless governed); identify recurring complaint themes monthly; correct factual misconceptions where appropriate; track response rate. Audit each target source and record current wording/state: TripAdvisor. Correct only the sources where facts are missing, conflicting, or outdated. Do not change measurement methodology. Store completion evidence (canonical policy summary, sources reviewed, sources corrected, URLs/screenshots, completion date). Notify Dealality of completion so the next monitoring period can check the expected signal without assuming causation.
